![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14095109/assets/f531f2467284ef84e0af0758a8e8554f1e5f72ea08d30d0b80c83076fbe5d7a3.png)

Evaluate ${\int }_{C}(x+\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡\pi y)\,\text{d}x,$ where $C$ is the path traversed along the line segment from the point $(1,0)$ to the point $(2,1),$ as shown above.
worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y={\int }_{a}^{b}f(r(t))\,\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t.
$$

The curve $C$ is a line segment with endpoints $(1,0)$ and $(2,1).$ It can be parametrized as 

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨(1+t(2-1)),\,(0+t(1-0))⟩ \\  & =⟨1+t,\,t⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

where $0\le t\le 1.$

Computing $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1+t)=1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $f(x,y)=x+\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡\pi y$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =(1+t)+\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡\pi t \\  & =1+t+\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡\pi t.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now evaluate the integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}f(r(t))\,\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(1+t+\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡\pi t)\cdot 1\cdot \text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}1+t+\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡\pi t\,\text{d}t \\  & ={[t+\frac{{t}^{2}}{2}+\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi t]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(1+\frac{{1}^{2}}{2}+\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi )-(0+\operatorname{sin}⁡0) \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
